subject.title: fix: harden security and release integrity

question: Should trusted private-network callbacks remain supported through an explicit opt-in policy, or should this PR intentionally make public-only callbacks a breaking upgrade contract?
rationale: Both directions are technically possible, but choosing between compatibility for internal deployments and a stricter unconditional SSRF boundary is a security and product contract that automation cannot decide safely.

options.title: Add secure opt-in compatibility
options.body: Keep public-only egress as the default and add a narrow trusted-private allowlist or policy with DNS pinning, upgrade documentation, and focused tests.

options.title: Approve public-only cutover
options.body: Treat private callbacks as intentionally unsupported, document the breaking upgrade behavior, and provide proof that affected operators receive an actionable failure path.

recommendation.title: Add secure opt-in compatibility
recommendation.body: Keep public-only egress as the default and add a narrow trusted-private allowlist or policy with DNS pinning, upgrade documentation, and focused tests.

likelyOwner.reason: They own the current callback hardening implementation and are assigned as the repository member driving this PR.
